previous_subtask_patterns: ^move to the top of the (?:right|left)-side target(?: at <[0-9]+, [0-9]+>)? for the (?:first|second|third) time$
success_conditions: The physical right-side target is bound to the circular target in the image-left half of the fixed front camera, and the physical left-side target is bound to the circular target in the image-right half.
The grounded point for a right-side instruction lies on the image-left circular target; the grounded point for a left-side instruction lies on the image-right circular target.
Later cycles preserve the same two physical side bindings instead of swapping coordinates when an old target remains highlighted.
insufficient_evidence: The side name is inferred from whichever target is currently red without checking its stable front-camera side.
A right-side instruction points into the image-right half or a left-side instruction points into the image-left half.
The previous target's coordinate is reused for the opposite side in the next half-cycle.

required_checks.question: Does the named physical side match the task-level front-camera binding: right target in image-left, left target in image-right?
Is the proposed point visibly centered on the circular target in the correct image half, rather than on the opposite target, cube, or button?
Is this the same physical side binding used for this side earlier, without swapping because of a lingering highlight?
